item.description:
## 一、这场演讲在无意间宣告了"科斯企业理论"的死亡
Ronald Coase 在 1937 年问了一个问题：**如果市场这么高效，为什么还需要公司？** 他的答案是——因为"交易成本"（协调、谈判、信息传递）在公司内部比在市场上更低，所以我们把活动圈进公司这个"层级"里。
Michael 讲的整套东西，其实是在说：**AI 让内部协调成本趋近于零**。当协调不再需要"人作为中转"，公司这个组织形态存在的经济学根基就被抽掉了。他讲"中层管理消失"只是表象；真正在消失的是"公司作为一种降低交易成本的容器"这个概念本身。未来最锋利的组织可能不是"更小的公司"，而是"一个人 + 一个 company brain + 一群被临时召集的边缘人类"——这已经不是公司，是**一种新的经济单位**，我们暂时还没有名字给它。
## 二、"夜里修 bug 的第二个 agent"其实是硅基的 REM 睡眠
他描述的那个"头炸了"的时刻——第一层 agent 白天做查询，第二层 agent 夜里扫失败日志、发 PR 修复——**这几乎是神经科学里 REM 睡眠记忆巩固机制的一比一复刻**。人脑在睡眠

item.title: [Business of Sport] Does Bezos’s Money Matter to Liverpool, LIV Golf’s $300m Miracle, & The €4.2bn World of MotoGP
item.dc:creator: Business of Sport
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

三个反直觉的系统性观察

一、UEFA 的"温柔一刀"：真正的权力从不需要投票

表面上看，这是 UEFA、Concacaf、AFC 联手对抗 Infantino 的一次民主政治操作。但更深层的真相是：UEFA 根本不需要 106 票。它拥有的是"存在性权力"——顶级球员的合同都在欧洲俱乐部手里，没有 UEFA 参与的世界杯只是一场业余表演。这封信最锋利的一句话是"FIFA 和它所服务的机构（institutions it serves）"——一个动词的翻转，把 FIFA 从"上级"降格为"仆人"。

这里有一个让人意外的类比：这与苹果和 App Store 开发者的关系惊人相似。平台方（FIFA/Apple）掌握着表面上的规则制定权，但真正的价值创造者（联赛/开发者）一旦联合起来威胁"另建生态"，平台立刻虚弱。Infantino 的错误不是贪婪，而是忘记了自己是被授权者而非授权者。而 Montagliani 若上位，将成为足球史上第一个"被明确告知自己是傀儡"的 FIFA 主席——这是一种独特的、被公开化的权力结构。

二、Liverpool、LIV Golf、MotoGP 三则新闻背后的同一个隐秘主线：资本正在从"买入体育"转向"重构体育的收入结构"

这三则看似无关的故事，其实共享一个底层逻辑——在营收监管和成本约束时代，钱本身失去了直接购买胜利的能力。

  • Bezos 进入 Liverpool 不重要，因为 2003 年那种"砸钱买冠军"的时代结束了。真正重要的是——他能否推动 Anfield 拆掉重建成 10 万人体育场？这是一个跨越足球、房地产、城市规划、文化认同的复合决策。
  • LIV Golf 用 60 亿美元失败的事，某个私募 2.5 亿要重来——这在数学上是荒谬的，除非你理解私募基金必须部署已募集的资本，否则收不到管理费。所以这可能不是投资，而是一次"资金必须找家"的仪式性动作。BC Partners 同时持有 Bryson DeChambeau 的经纪公司 GSE，这个"轮中之轮"的结构告诉我们：当直接投资无法自洽时，间接利益（agency fees、面子、PIF 的关系）会成为交易的真正定价机制。
  • MotoGP 的成本帽争论最反直觉："少花钱能让你的资产更值钱"——这个道理连很多足球俱乐部老板都无法理解。Charlie 举 Brentford vs Stoke 的例子极其精彩：花钱多的输给花钱少的，因为约束创造了效率、效率创造了系统性价值溢价。

三、跨领域连接：LIV Golf 的"员工持股 = 未来价值"叙事，与 WeWork 员工股权、初创公司期权画饼、甚至加密货币的"Community Ownership"是同一个心理骗局

Scott O'Neal 把"球员成为多数股权持有人"包装成历史性胜利——但你测算一下：如果 Bryson 用 5 亿美元现金合同换 2% 股权，LIV 需要卖到 250 亿美元他才能打平。这是一个天文数字，超过整个 PGA Tour 的估值。

这个话术的模板你在硅谷听过一万次： - "别拿高工资，拿期权，将来上市你就财务自由了" - "别要即时报酬，加入我们的社区代币，你就是主人" - "别争年薪，加入我们的合伙人计划，长期回报无限"

当一个组织用"未来价值"替代"当下现金"，通常意味着它当下无法支付、未来也大概率无法兑现。 LIV 的球员们正在被邀请签一份"精心设计的自我贬值合同"——这是 Adam Neumann、Sam Bankman-Fried 和 Scott O'Neal 之间惊人相似的叙事技术。

而这三件事共同揭示的元观察是：2020 年代的体育商业，最重要的技能已经不是找钱，而是识别"哪种钱能真正改变系统结构"。Bezos 的钱不改变 Liverpool 的结构（因为不进俱乐部），BC 的钱不改变 LIV 的结构（因为量级不够），但 Liberty 的钱可能改变 MotoGP 的结构（如果他们能推行成本帽）。结构性的钱 > 名义上更大的钱——这是现代体育资本的第一原理。

📝 转录文本

Does Bezos's Money Matter to Liverpool, LIV Golf's $300m Miracle, & The €4.2bn World of MotoGP

开场：本期看点提要

The question that I really started to ask myself, Charlie, was, does it really matter if it's Jeff Bezos? Does it really matter if you get one of the world's richest people in? Does it really matter if you bring all these billionaires in when you've already got billionaire owners in there? This feels to me like it's Fenway taking money off the table. We're already break even on our investment. We've already sold some minority. Now, let's take in a real proper chunk of change here.

It's one of the most profound far-reaching statements that I've seen in the football industry in my time. FIFA, you are only there at our behest. You're only there as long as we want you to be there. And if we don't want you to be there, that's just the way it will go.

Live Golf is dead. Liv has failed with a $6 billion injection of capital. What makes you think you could achieve something with 250 million that you couldn't with six?

Look at the recent acquisition of Moto GP by Liberty Media, who of course acquired Formula 1 10 years ago or so. Those teams are currently trading at about 50 million bucks. Watch this space. This sport in the next 5 to 10 years could become something big.

Substack 预告

Before we start, a quick reminder for those of you that haven't yet joined us on Substack to get yourselves over there. If you love or even just like this show and want to see bonus segments, written pieces, polls, behind-the-scenes access, and events, there's only one place to go. Come and see what it's all about. It's live now. Check out the link in the bio, and we'll see you there.

主持人寒暄

Good morning, Charlie. Wow, what a show. Someone looks like they could be on holiday. someone is on holiday, but taking time out for um the breakdown, which is of course never a chore. Always a pleasure to see my Charlie Junior's cheerful face grafting away in London. But yeah, I thought I'd um bring a bit of my Caribbean get up to to the show this week because it is I know you're arriving in Cornwall shortly, Charlie Junior. Um and I can tell you in advance it is pretty Caribbean down here. Even down to the rum punches and the rum bar on PS Beach, which I know that um is a place which you would never frequent in a million years.

Well, no. Look, it's it's all you we could call it the birthplace of the break. Well, like the earliest seeds of the breakdown. We should honor it.

Well, we will. I'm sure we will. Um and try and make sure that we're not we're not doing another edition of the breakdown straight afterwards because that might be slightly slow paced, but um today is not going to be slow paced because we have an awful lot to get through.

第一部分：FIFA 风波与 UEFA 的反击

背景回顾

The news keeps on coming and obviously in the last few weeks we've been covering in depth um the FIFA scandal um that followed from the FIFA Ford Enterprises um gambit played by Janney Afantino or about to be played by Gianino until it was revealed rather ahead of its time and and knocked down very quickly. And we speculated two weeks ago that this was a time for UEFA to step up. Um and then we reported last week that UEFA had indeed stepped up by basically threatening to boycott FIFA organized competitions um unless significant changes um were upcoming to the way in which FIFA is run. And and frankly they made it pretty clear that that future was not going to be able to include Giani Infantino who's up for reelection next March.

I mean the letter that uh was put out since we last recorded between UEFA Conquer Calf and um the AFC Asian Football Confederation is probably the most notable uh point of of what's happened in the last few days isn't it alongside this because when we've talked about it before it's always been about well UEFA can take their stance but who comes with them and you mentioned I think to me the last time that Mont Victor Montigani the head of conquer was uh not only you know supporter of this but also the likely candidate that would stand against Infantino in the next elections.

UEFA 三方联合声明全文朗读

So, they have written a letter. Now, Charlie, I I've actually got it here. It was a very long one, right? So, I've I've condensed it down a little bit. It's still quite long, but I think in the context of all of our conversations and also with our love of statements, I'm going to rebrand it. We've only ever really from the start, we've had an HP and we've had a Belgian Football Federation. And I'm going to call a third tranch of statement for us to use for the UEFA statement because there's a kind of poetic license to even some of this in how they emphasize their points. I'm going to read it out for everyone so so that you can understand because it is it's it's a relatively groundbreaking moment particularly in the um well I would say in the future of FIFA but it goes like this. It goes:

Dear football family, football is the world's greatest shared passion. It belongs to no individual and no institution. It belongs to the players, the fans, the clubs, the member associations, and every institution entrusted with safeguarding its future.

The growth over the past decade has been real. But that progress was never the work of one individual. The expanded tournaments, the awarding of the 2030 and 34 FIFA World Cups, the distribution and resources of associations, these were shared achievements.

This is not about money. The confederations have already called for the responsible distribution of FIFA's vast existing reserves to further strengthen investment in the development of member associations. This is about something more fundamental. The integrity of the game and the integrity of those elected to lead it.

Leadership in football is not a possession. When trust is broken through deception, when an individual places himself above the collective that entrusted him with the authority, that duty has been abandoned.

FIFA's recent letter to the vice presidents and 211 member associations acknowledges that mistakes were made in the process. It treats this as a failure of communication when what football witnessed was a failure of judgment. It did not acknowledge that the proposal itself was inherently wrong. There remains no recognition that attempting to sell an interest in the FIFA World Cup was a profound failure of judgment, not just a procedural misstep, but a fundamental breach of trust with the very institutions FIFA exists to serve.

FIFA has also committed to presenting a full report on these events to the FIFA Council. Once again, failing to recognize that proper governance in the face of such a profound lack of judgment would require that such a review be conducted by a fully independent third party, not by FIFA itself, its staff, or by any stakeholder within football. The FIFA administration should play no role in conducting the review. As per previous correspondents, all relevant documents and records must be preserved.

FIFA's own letter also confirms that only one elected official was present at the leadership meeting in Morocco. There is silence where there should be accountability, distance where there should be openness. That was the poetic bit I quite enjoyed. Um there these are not qualities football deserves in its leadership. That is why we have taken this stance. Not lightly and not alone, but together and out of a duty for the game we serve.

Yours sincerely, Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, the AFC president. Victor Montaglani the Concacaf president and Alexander Ceferin the UEFA president.

This is the first time the players will be the majority equity holders in a major sporting tour. Equity means value. What what value? What what value are these players going to have moving forward? This business has no value right now. So, if you're transferring cash ow to players to equity, that's assuming that one day those players are going to be better off than they would be if they had got that cash for them to actually look at this as a really good deal.

I don't know about you, there's nothing to me that says you can get rid of all of the liabilities that LIV has now. You can turn it around with $250 to $300 million. You can create value on top of that to make a percentage of that equity worth something to all of these players so that eventually one day you can miraculously find a buyer who's going to pay you something significant enough to give those players back a proper portion of cash.

Let's play this out if it's Bryson's contract, right? Let's say let's just use the big numbers, right? If he got a 500 million deal, which was being talked about previously as him renewing on LIV, let's say he got a 2% ownership of the whole of LIV. LIV would need to sell for 25 billion for him to back a like equity model over his cash model to make that worthwhile. So it's a complete like fazi fallacy, whatever we want to call it to suggest that this equity model for the players is a good thing.

BC Partners 与 GSE Worldwide 的"轮中之轮"

We have to say this with a big reported in the golf world. It's widely reported that BC Partners, which is a P private equity credit firm, are the investor. Now, they supposedly have said that the continuation and participation of some of those key players is important to their investment. So, you're going to have to find a way to keep those players other than just pay them huge sums of cash.

I'm very keen to see how they manage to do that. I'm going to massively speculate, but if PIF owe a huge amount of money to some of those players on contracts, I could see maybe a settlement agreement with some of those players, which would still give them a significant amount of money and a significant enough portion to keep them involved in a LIV structure for x amount of time that would allow BC partners to take that majority stake and not have to worry about serious injections of cash just from player for player contracts. That's huge speculation on my side, but that's the only way that I could see that happening.

More importantly, Charlie, I had a little look um at BC Partners.n Do you know another big investment that they made in sport? Do you know what that that was?

No. Who was that?

They invested in a company called GSE Worldwide. Now GSSE Worldwide is a big sports marketing representation talent agency. Do you know who GSSE's major client is on the golfing front?

Bryson. So the same company that has invested significant cash in the represent in one of the representation agencies for Bryson DeChambeau is going to be the company reportedly that puts money into LIV golf.

Yeah. And this is going to be my speculation was that when when I heard that there was a supposed investor into LIV Golf, I sort of felt it's likely to be some an entity or somebody or something who could be lent on on who or who would have some sort of ulterior motive. You know, I was going to speculate that it might be someone close to the Trump family. Many of the LIV events are played at Trump venues, for instance, or somebody who might want to be on PIF's right side who comes in with a face saver um which enables the whole thing to continue.

um you know so it that that kind of wheels within wheels type um thing like you remember when it came to um the whole TV deals around the club world cup and yeah the circularity between Saudi winning the contract to to host the World Cup at the same time as as Saudi and DAZN paying what didn't seem to be an obviously good value amount for the TV rights for the club world cup which enabled Infantino to say the club world cup was a success Yes, there was a sort of circularity going on.

私募资本必须"部署"的宿命

So I sus I don't know my my instinct is since there is no business case that can be made for it whatsoever. Um my instinct is is it will be one of those wheels within wheels type transactions where there's enough face saving benefits slash um agency benefits slash side benefits slash being good friends with PIF benefits because one thing that is true Charlie is a vast amount of money has been raised in the last three years by the major private equity firms to invest in sport and that money has to find a home right and that's what's driving some asset valuations to slightly strange levels in around the sort of fringes of sport which is that once they've raised the money the only way which they then attract management fees on deploying that money is when they actually make investments. So even if the investment might be a bit bit high on the riskreward scheme um higher than might normally be attractive it can still be better than not deploying the money at all.

Um so jolly I agree with that but interestingly BC is not an Apollo a KKR an Ares right one of one of the big US funds let's say at 5 plus billion where you know okay I I I still personally I still think it's mad other people may disagree but as you've said there deploying that capital is is actually tough in this market at that when you have that amount of it and you've got a number of organizations operating so you know could you have done something with one of them potentially the number is what it would actually take to invest properly in this if you were going to have a crack at it.

I mean, 250 to 300 million, you know, all I'm looking at is what's going to be the future injections. Just like you would, John, if you're buying a football club, right, it's not about necessarily what you pay for it. You know that it's about what you're going to have to put into it to continue to not just run it properly, but build value into it so that one day you can hopefully make some money out of it.

And this is the big change, right? LIV is now going to have to operate as a sovereign wealth entity into a private capital entity. Yeah. And the minute like you go from that to that, money is important.

I keep I kept checking myself going, "Hang on, Charlie, you always criticize people just for looking at the monetary value of things. What about the secondary nature?" You just touched on maybe some of the secondary natures here, but I don't really see the secondary nature for a BC of doing this if they if they didn't genuinely believe they could make some value out of it.

But, you know, I was asking myself, why did players come and play for LIV in the first place? The only reason was for cash, right? So, you even just from a motivations perspective, you Well, actually, I say that that's a lie. Dustin, as I've just said, Dustin Johnson said that he was playing a bit less and he loved that as well. and got more time. So, you know, find the package was was good, but the majority of it, let's not kid ourselves, was the huge fees that that that a lot of the players got. It was the you get paid for turning up, not just for making a cut.

They're saying that, you know, now prize pools will go down to $10 million an event. They were at $25 to $30 million an event. You're not going to get the major signon fees. Your equity, as we've discussed previously, is is is only worth anything in a few in what, five to 10 years time if you eventually manage to put something together. And even then, it's probably not going to reach the cash that you thought you were going to get when you came in. There's a lot of it that to me, I I I just don't understand it. I I genuinely don't.

And I think Scott O'Neal, look, to be fair to him, look, he's the CEO and his job is to try and keep this thing alive and he's going to put across a narrative and talk about it in ways that anyone who is slightly critical of this whole thing will pull apart like like we've just done. I don't blame him for that. It's the reality of his position.

So yeah, if I can leave it on one thing, there's a craziness to it from a financial perspective. The thing I really worry about is who's getting in the players ears going, "Hey guys, you know, this is an amazing equity scheme for you. Be a part of this. Honestly, it's all going to be good. You owed that money, but we're going to give you more equity. I hope there's really good people around them, the ones that are getting promised a lot of this value to to put some of that into context and and build a realistic picture of it because otherwise you can see an unfortunate position for a few of them coming um coming to fruition."

第四部分：MotoGP 的 €42 亿新赛道

一次真正意义上的深度剖析

moving on from an uninvestable um sport um in sporting entity as we see it anyway and you know very happy if anyone from LIV wants to come on and explain to us why we're wrong um we'd always be delighted into an into an event or a series um that is uh in a much more interesting spot right so last weekend was the British Moto GP the Grand Prix the motorcycling Grand Prix at Silverstone um that's only one event on the Moto GP circuit is and Charlie and I thought this would be a good moment to do a deep dive into Moto GP um and where it's at, where it's come from, where it's going to um and you know, this is just at that time of the year when we we've just had the French and the Italian and the British um and I think the Spanish the sort of big legacy Grand Prix have now happened. So we can take a health check on where they are, but also look at um the recent acquisition of Moto GP by Liberty Media, who of course acquired Formula 1 10 years ago or so.

Yeah. Well done. Uh yeah, look, I think the thing to say is this is a huge sport with a massive fan base and great history and there's only a certain amount that we'll be able to cover in in 15 or so minutes. So, you know, we can we can develop this going forward. I think it is a really interesting um story to explore.

€42 亿的价格与全球观众结构

Now, not least because Liberty have bought it for €4.2 billion reportedly. Uh I say reportedly Carlos Espa who's the chief uh sporting officer um who I have spoken to said that on a show that that we did with them. So, you know, if we can take pretty accurately that Liberty paid 4.2 billion for um Moto GP, there must be some significant value.

You would assume that a company riding the wave that Liberty are and the reputation they have through what they've done with Formula 1 where they see significant value in this sport. Now I like me Charlie when I first did a Moto GP show I must admit I didn't know a huge amount about Moto GP other than Valentino Rossi and Mark Marquez and some crazy crashes that I'd seen online and maybe you know when I was younger uh you know a few glimpses of races. there had never been something that had properly captured me and I think that's probably down to just the wealth of sport that's available and you know if it was a motorsport formula 1 had been the thing I'd covered but when I did get into it I really started to appreciate you know how big this sport was

and I don't necessarily just mean big from the breadth of fan base I mean big from the depth of fan base the audience for Moto GP globally and you know we're always careful how we say these but let's just say it's over 600 million people last year I think was it over three 3.6 6 million spectators went into the 22 um races throughout the year. There's a real geographical element to it. Spain, Italy, France host a third of the the events, the the the Grand Prix, and they are a huge portion of that fan base.

So, you got depth in some areas, but you have little global breadth if we want for a sport. Now, if you're looking at a value, that's a concern potentially or it's a huge opportunity. You can see Liberty looking at that and going, if there's great attention for this in those markets, fantastic. That's a call we can build off. But there's a massive opportunity for us to go and take this um into into new areas.

与 15 年前的 F1 何其相似

What does that remind you of? It reminds me it reminds me of Formula 1 15 years ago where you had an enormous European audience um and where America basically wasn't interested at all. Um and where they'd lost the the threads a bit in in Latin America as well. and Liberty made the bet that they could crack the US and that in so doing they would totally change the business dynamics of the sport.

I think it's worth noting that um Liberty are not the first major financial institution to own Mo um Moto GP. Um it was actually originally bought um by CVC back in 1998 and that's before CVC owned Formula 1. Um and the only reason why CVC gave it up, which is quite interesting, is is that when they then bought Formula 1, um the European Commission said that they would have to divest themselves of Moto GP because only Moto GP and Formula 1 would give them too much dominance within the motorsport space within the European Union. So, I'm not quite sure how the the same rules haven't applied this time because obviously Liberty have been allowed to buy both Moto GP and Formula 1.

Anyhow, um they bought it. CVC bought it for 80 million bucks back in in the 1990s. Um, and they sold it to Bridgepoint, another private equity firm, once they were forced to divest of it for 500 million bucks. So, they made a good turn over seven or eight years. And then Bridgepoint have held on to it for the thick end of 20 years. They sold a bit of minority along the way to then exited at four billion bucks.

Right now, it might sound like 500 million to 4 billion is a great return, but actually that's not how a private equity firm would see it over 20 years. 20 years is effectively three fund cycles. So, you're talking about what we call continuation vehicles effectively where it would have been in a Bridgepoint fund. It wouldn't have been deemed ready for sale. So, it would have been put into the next Bridgepoint fund at a certain slightly higher valuation and then into the next Bridgepoint fund. So, I mean, it's not it's not a bad return for Bridgepoint over that period, but it certainly doesn't suggest that they were able to do anything with it that really changed the mold, particularly given that in general terms, sports business valuations during that time went through the ceiling in many other um different areas.

So effectively, Liberty are betting that as kind of sports and media operators, which Bridgepoint aren't. They're a private equity firm. as sports and business specialists that they are going to be able to achieve something that CVC and Bridgepoint were not able to do which is to turn the the the sort of latent um demand for motorcycling and motor sort of sports but two-wheeled variety around the world and coagulate it into Moto GP.

So if you look for instance there's a lot of demand for motorcycle racing in the US. Um I've seen motorcycle racing in the US. It's just not Moto GP.

缺乏"跨界明星"的困境

Now, Moto GP itself, Charlie, is a as a brand name has not been in existence for all that long. It was it was around sort of 25 30 years ago that it was changed. Up until that point, there were various different championships of prestige, frankly. Um, of which the top one, generally speaking, was 500cc. The 500cc world championship was reckoned to be the the marquee, the blue chip event.

And when I was a young whippers snapper in growing up in this country in the UK, the biggest motorsports celebrity in the country, two wheels or four wheels was a man called Barry Sheene. Um who was the 500cc double world champion. He was an immensely charismatic Cockney who was, you know, used to smoke on the grid before starting the races, had beautiful girlfriends, was a real sort of high living James Hunt style type figure. Um, but that gives some idea that when Sheene was racing at Silverstone, you had crowds there that at the time were absolutely the same as for a Formula 1 Grand Prix, maybe even bigger. I mean, that he was a bigger, he was a more famous person than Nigel Mansell was in the UK at the time.

Um, so effectively what I think the sport has lacked somewhat in the last 10 to 15 years are marketable stars outside of two maybe Valentino Rossi um, and Mark Marquez being two who even I would recognize and go okay yeah those are big names but they haven't been able to develop unlike Formula 1 those types of rivalries and charismatic people who do stuff outside of the track and the whole thing becomes a sort of great sort of um uh sort of show. Um it's very much carried on being something for the enthusiasts.

So I'm going to be really interested to see the Liberty playbook. How much of the Formula 1 playbook are they going to apply to this Charlie?

Yeah, and let's be honest, right? That that's what Formula 1 removed the helmet. Sorry, Liberty Media Drive Survivor. He said Liberty Media decided that Drive Survive is going to be a great tool for them to do a lot of this. They removed the helmet from the drivers. We got to know everything about them plus the people behind it. Interest grew because it was a human story. It was people. It was sport. It was everything packaged into one. Plus, you know, high intensity, incredibly dangerous, exciting. Well, I say exciting, sometimes exciting sport.

MotoGP 客观上比 F1 更刺激也更危险

Moto GP is insane. You know, races can't really be longer than 45 minutes to an hour because the intensity on the bodies and the physicality that is required to race some of these is is so intense.

Moto GP is both objectively more exciting and more dangerous. There's much more overtaking because obviously the size of the motorcycles compared to a car makes it more feasible to overtake and because the drivers are so obviously physically exposed to the track, it's extremely dangerous. So, if you're into adrenaline and speed and real daredevils, etc., Moto GP really should be more your thing than Formula 1, which has become, you know, a driver enclosed within a car. as you say, once the helmet's on, there's not much you can see about that particular driver.

I mean, is you motorcycling is a more physical sport where they have to wrestle the bikes around the place. Um, it is unbelievably exciting. I've been to um Silverstone. I think maybe it was Donington, actually, to watch a Moto GP event or 500cc, I can't remember which one it was, 20, 25 years ago. And I've never seen anything like it. I mean, it was it was so adrenaline-fueled. I mean, the whole thing was, you know, you could see the the the the drivers fairly close up.

Um, so it is an interesting sports mystery as to how it's never quite managed to crack, not never, but how outside of certain core markets, particularly Italy and Spain, it hasn't quite managed to crack the broader market.

车队结构与惊人的估值裂谷

That that's got to be the belief of Liberty. I'm really excited to see who comes in as potential buyers of teams if they're up for sale, which have a quick look at the teams, Charlie. It's a good point, right? So, so basically ju just just to summarize to to people there are 11 teams, five of which are what we call factory teams. So that's where the manufacturer themselves has the team just like in Formula 1 where you have Mercedes um uh and so on and so forth. In in motorcycling you have Ducati, you have Aprilia, you have um Honda, you have Yamaha who own their own teams. They then also supply engines and technology to six independent teams. And those teams currently, which obviously are the ones that can trade because the factory ones by definition, well, they could trade. We've seen that with Mercedes recently, but that not currently so much the case. But those teams are currently trading at about 50 million bucks.

Now, if we think that Formula 1 teams right now, Charlie, are being valued at well over a billion minimum up to six billion, right? So you're probably the cheapest Formula One team you're probably getting is about one and a half billion now, right? I think you'd say bottom of the grid.

So right. So So the Mercedes and Mercedes valuation in our first show was 6 billion is what George Kurtz bought into it at 6 billion. We just talked about Liverpool being valued at 4.5 billion.

Yeah. Right. Um but we've also noted, Charlie, that prior to Liberty's takeover, the smaller Formula 1 teams were being valued at 100 to 150 million bucks.

Well, yeah. I mean, and that's and that's generous, Charlie, right? I mean, if we're being really honest, they were worth pretty much nothing if you're looking at the mid-2010s. I mean, they they could barely survive.

But on that point, you know, that's I mean, that's the key element. You know, they were businesses and underperforming businesses. They've been built into franchises. And if you're looking at what you got a Moto GP opportunity now, can you make these businesses? Can you turn them into those similar franchises?

Now that price I always look at like the gap between total asset value and then the you know the key components of what makes a Moto GP i.e. the teams you got pretty much 100x difference between what some of the teams are trading for and what the total value is. Now I remember when I first saw this I was like someone surely got this wrong. Someone's got this wrong. One's a massively overpriced one's massively underpriced.

the more I've got into it, you know, I think to be honest, yes, maybe maybe four, you know, plus billion was punchy from from a buy price. Actually, the economics of it, I don't think were I can't I actually don't have it right in front of me. I think it was about 9 8 n times revenue. The top end of of sports valuations, if we're looking purely at that metric, not ridiculous. The teams, however, that makes them viable. if they can put an ecosystem together where you get really smart and exciting investment coming in and deploying cash alongside what they can do as Moto GP central you've got the foundations for a for a good organization

关键之战：成本帽

now they don't have cost caps that's so we we also we talk about drive to survive but as we've also mentioned on many in occasion what made Formula 1 really big and a lot of the business it is today was the implementation of a cost cap because it just meant that investors didn't have to come in lose bucket loads of cash to win things they don't have that in Moto GP

But It's kind of a subtle change. And I spoke to Carlos about this on the show. I think he said a €10 million euro spend will get you 0.05 seconds gain. So he said it's not even if you spend ridiculous amounts of money trying to improve the speeds of these bikes, it's not actually going to give you a huge advantage to get a second ahead, which would be a huge advantage, you would need to spend 200 plus million.

I think that's special pleading from Espa in in he knows that it would be much more attractive with a cost cap, but they haven't been able to get the manufacturers to sign up to it yet, which is just where Formula 1 was before. So, he sort of says, well, you know, yeah, okay, we don't have a cost cap, but it doesn't really make that much difference. It makes a huge difference.

And the reason it makes a difference, Charlie, is something that you mentioned in relation to buying football clubs um earlier and is if you can have business certainty that over a five-year period, your entity is not going to lose money on an operational basis, you as the new owner of that team can plan your investment around marketing. You can actually say, "Right, we we know we've got the operational side locked down because I think they actually receive from Moto GP. each team receives about 8 million in TV revenue distribution, right? So, let's just say that they had a a cost cap of of 10 million or 15 million and you say, "Right, okay, we're getting 8 million from Central. We're then getting five or six 7 million from sponsorship on a on a reliable basis." Okay. Right. So, we are now operationally break even. So, any money that I now invest into my team is going to go into marketing my team and try and make it into the franchise, which then enables the valuation to rise.

And without the cost cap, you never quite know where the next frontier might lead. If one of the other teams then gets a big new advantage where you might have to then follow to be competitive and without being competitive, you don't have your attractive franchise and so on and so forth. So for me this is going to be one of the big battlefields um for Liberty in fact over the next two to three to four years is persuading all of the teams guys all of your valuations are going to massively increase if you agree to a cost cap.

Brentford vs Stoke：老板们最难懂的道理

It totally like screws with my mind that people don't understand this and we'll have to come on next weeks. haven't had time this week to cover um uh football cost caps um where there's big news flow at the moment is I speak to football club owners who simply cannot comprehend that losing less money would make their entity more valuable. They literally can't understand it. They say, "Yeah, but if I lose less money, that means I'll be less good at football. And if I'm less good at football, then I'll be worth less money." No, no, sorry. The cost cap applies to everybody. It doesn't just apply to you. It applies to everybody. and therefore everybody becomes worth more money. Yeah, but what happens if I want to beat this other team? Forget it. Doesn't matter. You're going to become worth three to four times as much even without beating that team.

Now, if Moto GP can get that into the franchises, the franchises will rise in value or the the teams will rise in value. And it will also mean a re a reallocation of capital away from spending on trying to get faster into actually becoming better marketed, better businesses, etc. they'll be able to hire better executives to run their commercial and marketing side and all this type of stuff. So I I I think this is

it just makes you more efficient, right, as well. It actually improves your technology investment to an extent because you're more refined in what you're doing. You're not just sping loads of money to try and do stuff.

Again, taking it back to football, Charlie, this is why I call sort of like the differential between like Brentford and Stoke, right? Whoever runs Stoke knows that they've got an owner in the Coates family who own bet 365 who are basically willing to spaf as much money as they possibly can find on Stoke City because they just don't care and it's their club and they want everyone in the town to think they're great people. Right. And then you got Brentford where where it's one person who is a wealthy person but not a billionaire. Um who every pound counts, everything has to get measured. There has to be efficiency in every single thing they do. Who wins at football compet between Brentford and Stoke? the ones with the billionaire spafing money or the ones who are run on a tight reign. The ones who run on a tight reign, which again is the other thing which is very hard for owners to understand within sport.

Anyhow, the long and the short of it is is I think both you and I are quite excited by Moto GP as a proposition and with what and with what Liberty can do for it.

Silverstone 上座率与全球赛事对比

I enjoyed it this morning as I was getting I I know when you're excited by something because I get loads of messages and screenshots of articles and I think, "Oh, he's in a hole here. He's enjoying it." Um the Moto GP. So, so the event that we had at Silverstone at the weekend, you know, should we say statistically? I've seen read some some negative commentary around it, you know, UK and around the attendance.

This is around the attendance.

Around the attendances. Yeah.

Yeah. The attendances were about 100,000 over 3 days with 45 odd thousand on the main day. Listen, by general standards, that's bloody good, right? But it's true to say that in the in case of the British Grand Prix that is somewhat down from its peak of about 150,000.

At the same time, not to be too anglocentric about it, the French Grand Prix has been breaking records up to 300,000 now on a reliable basis every year is going there and the Italians are up to almost 200,000 and the Spanish are up to almost 250,000. So you are seeing massive attendances just with a little asterisk that says I think that Britain is suffering here from not having had a very preeminent motorcyclist for quite some time. Carl Fogarty who was the world superbikes champion which which is a different series was the last big English British motorcycling champion really and that was 15 20 years ago. Now we got Cal Crutchlow who rides and who is a good rider but he hasn't managed to break into that upper echelon of British sporting celebrity. Whereas if you look at Spain and France during that last 15 year period they've had competitive riders

completely and that was why I wanted to bring that up because I thought if you know for us and any listeners in the UK if you've seen any articles on this in the last few days it could have had a negative spin on it. If we look at it and as I said take away the English perspective look at it as a whole it's actually doing quite exciting stuff and the audience demographics are quite exciting as well which I think Liberty would like. Um, you know, over half of the global fan base remains under the age of 35 based on the data they've done, which is hugely appealing for a sport at the moment. The viewership grew on average by 9% across each Grand Prix last year and the social following over 60 million followers. So, you know, there's lots in there to like and hey, look, Liberty had done great things previously, as we've said. Who's to say they won't do it again? I think some really interesting.

They've only just they bought it a year ago. So I I I like watch this space. This this sport in the next 5 to 10 years could become something big.

Completely agree.

结束语与 Substack 转场

There we go. So I think we're now heading over to Substack, aren't we Charlie?

Yes, we are going to head over we're going to head over to Substack now, Charlie, and we're going to start the first part of our Premier League season review. And it's not going to be just the normal who's going to score the most goals. We're going to do it from the business side because we get a lot of comments um across all the shows asking for our perspectives on some of the teams, the businesses they've been doing and the ownership structures, etc. It's very hard to touch on all of those in the main show. So, we thought let's go on and have a look at each club and how they stand going into the new season. So, come and join us on Substack. But if not, we will catch you next week with Charlie hopefully in another very exciting, colorful, flamboyant shirt.

## 三个反直觉的系统性观察
### 一、UEFA 的"温柔一刀"：真正的权力从不需要投票 表面上看，这是 UEFA、Concacaf、AFC 联手对抗 Infantino 的一次民主政治操作。但更深层的真相是：**UEFA 根本不需要 106 票**。它拥有的是"存在性权力"——顶级球员的合同都在欧洲俱乐部手里，没有 UEFA 参与的世界杯只是一场业余表演。这封信最锋利的一句话是"FIFA 和它所服务的机构（institutions it serves）"——一个动词的翻转，把 FIFA 从"上级"降格为"仆人"。
这里有一个让人意外的类比：**这与苹果和 App Store 开发者的关系惊人相似**。平台方（FIFA/Apple）掌握着表面上的规则制定权，但真正的价值创造者（联赛/开发者）一旦联合起来威胁"另建生态"，平台立刻虚弱。Infantino 的错误不是贪婪，而是**忘记了自己是被授权者而非授权者**。而 Montagliani 若上位，将成为足球史上第一个"被明确告知自己是傀儡"的 FIFA 主席——这是一种独特的、被公开化的权力结构。

💡 创造性洞见

一、最反直觉的观察：Katie 的"技术派"其实是一种认知节能装置

表面上，Katie 用月线随机指标、Fibonacci、Demark、200 日均线这些工具"读盘"。但仔细听她的语言逻辑，你会发现她真正在做的事，不是预测，而是授权自己不去思考噪音。

她反复说："价格已经包含了所有信息"、"我们不预测明天"、"指标本身就带滞后，这没关系"。

这其实是一种非常典雅的贝叶斯懒惰——她故意放弃对新闻、宏观、Clarity Act、硬件钱包被黑等信息的实时解读，把认知带宽全部集中在"趋势 + 动能 + 风险管理"三个变量上。这和一个禅修者的"注意力预算"分配几乎一样：决定不看什么，比决定看什么更重要。

对比一下：加密圈大部分分析师是"信息饕餮"，什么都想解释；Katie 是"信息素食者"，只吃价格这一种蛋白。这在一个 24/7、信息过载、叙事密度极高的加密市场里，反而成了一种结构性优势——不是因为她看得更准，而是因为她决策节奏更慢，被"叙事波动"绑架的概率更低。

二、跨领域连接：Hyperliquid 是加密世界的"英伟达"，Bitcoin 是"微软"

这是 Katie 在采访最后随口抛出的一句类比，但含金量极高：

"如果 Bitcoin 之于软件，那么 Hyperliquid 之于半导体。"

这个类比不是修辞，而是一种产业周期定位学。它意味着：

  • Bitcoin = 基础设施/操作系统层：波动率被"制度化"稀释，10x/100x 回报的时代正在结束（Katie 隐晦承认了这点），它开始扮演"加密里的 S&P 500"角色。
  • Hyperliquid = 前沿算力层：图形上和 NVDA、AI 半导体股高度同构——抛物线、剧烈回撤、但趋势线未破。它承载的不是"支付叙事"或"价值存储"，而是投机基础设施本身的复利（perp DEX 是加密世界的"生产工具"）。

真正意想不到的推论：如果这个类比成立，那 Hyperliquid 的下一个风险不是币价崩盘，而是"商品化"——就像半导体行业周期性遭遇的产能过剩。Steve 在访谈里点到了这一点（Kraken、Coinbase、247 主流指数交易），但没有连起来。Hyperliquid 目前的高溢价，来自它是唯一一个能在链上跑高频衍生品的"台积电级"节点，一旦合规化的 CEX 或 RWA 平台开始蚕食这个 niche，它的估值逻辑会从"AI 芯片"退化到"内存芯片"。

三、隐藏的系统性真相："平静"本身是一个信号，但方向和大多数人想的相反

标题说 "Bitcoin's Calm Could Be the Setup for Its Next Move Higher"——这听起来像是"暴风雨前的宁静"叙事。但 Katie 的技术框架其实在说一个更微妙的东西：

BVIV（Bitcoin 版 VIX）处于低位，且在一段下跌之后处于低位 —— 通常这是"complacency"（自满）的信号，应该看空。但 Katie 说："下跌之后的低波动率反而不那么令人担忧"。

翻译成系统语言：系统能量已经从"价格波动"转移到"时间消耗"。当一个市场既不上涨也不下跌，但波动率也在压缩，它其实在做一件事——用时间换空间，让持有者的心理成本超过机会成本，逼弱手离场。这在物理学上像"弹性势能积累"，在生态学上像"极相群落的表面静止"，在心理学上像"倦怠临界点"。

给你的意外洞见：加密市场最健康的状态，可能不是"上涨"，而是"让新闻失去价格弹性"。硬件钱包被黑损失九位数、Clarity Act 悬而未决、CPI 明天公布——Bitcoin 却一动不动。这不是"死气沉沉"，这是市场结构在做一次自我消化：把持币结构从"情绪驱动"重新洗牌为"策略驱动"。当散户对"每一个新闻都无反应"感到厌倦并离场时，就是 Katie 说的"major low"真正完成的时刻。

跨领域连接：这和生物学里的 punctuated equilibrium（间断平衡演化理论）几乎同构——大部分时间物种表现平静，真正的物种形成事件发生在极短的"结构重组"窗口。加密的每一个大周期，都不是"逐步上涨"，而是"长期沉默 → 突然重定价"。你现在看到的无聊，可能就是下一次重定价的酝酿层。

Same reason stocks and bonds would go up during COVID. It just — it is what it is.

Solana、XRP、Hyperliquid：主流山寨币解读

Solana

Um, all right. So let's quickly go through some of the other big tokens that I know people watching hold and pay attention to. Solana — we started discussing it a bit. As you mentioned, it had a good week. It had some decent ETF inflows. What are you seeing on that chart, if we could put it up?

Yeah, you'll see that it's been sort of advancing from what was a corrective phase. That was kind of interesting. And it's been tethered to its 50-day moving average to some degree, and now it seems to be wanting to pull away from it on improving short-term momentum.

If it does advance to that 200-day moving average, which is resistance just by the nature of it having like a psychological significance — so many eyes are on these 200-day moving averages, which really are just sort of a lagging gauge of the primary trend, but because they're so widely followed, they tend to have importance. So if we were to see that, that would mean that the consolidation or corrective action has, like, officially resolved to the upside, and would make Solana look a whole lot like a basing phase — a major low, if you zoomed out on the longer-term charts. And then we would start to focus on secondary resistance levels.

So you can see how it's more just fluid. We want to see, you know, bit by bit these positive catalysts continue to unfold. And in general, we have seen among the altcoins better momentum. So improved short-term momentum in addition to improved intermediate-term momentum, within the context of either an oversold or nearly oversold reading on a long-term basis. So not out of line with Bitcoin at all in the way it's been trading.

XRP：明显跑输

Okay. Um, well, one token that did not have a great week was XRP. So I'd love to kind of get a sense from you of what's happening there.

Well, and this is a good one to pull up because it shows that there is, of course, dispersion when you kind of pick apart the various names within the broader context. And we talk about — when we're talking about equities — like a stock-specific move. Well, this is like a crypto-specific move, clearly, where Ripple has been out of favor and correcting in a meaningful way still when others have caught a bid or stabilized, at least, right?

And now Ripple is testing some key support. And what we have found is that when support levels are broken — so meaning, for a short-term level, you're seeing a security close a couple times below that, or an intermediate-term level maybe a couple of weeks below that — that becomes something that tends to foster additional downside momentum.

So we're always respectful of breakouts and breakdowns, even if it's kind of against our better judgment and what we think should be happening, right? Because we don't want to let our biases sort of muddy the situation here. Right now what we know is that Ripple is testing support, pending confirmation of a breakdown, underperforming, and still hasn't really captured that momentum uptick that the rest have.

Yeah. Ripple's always a pretty fascinating one for me. It was bid up exceptionally high, especially during the 2024 presidential election. The company closely aligned itself with President Trump. And I forget the numbers, but I think it went up above $3, perhaps even higher. I mean, it did exceptionally well. And it was actually named in one of the — I think it was initially named in a tweet from President Trump about this national crypto stockpile — the one where he curiously forgot to mention Bitcoin underneath. I think someone reminded him about an hour later.

Um, I mean, Katie, you probably know this — a lot of people listening and watching know that in my earlier days as a journalist, I'd been critical of Ripple. Not for the company or what they did or the quality of their technology, but just for the amount of tokens held by Ripple Labs, the primary development team, and essentially my belief that there was not usage commensurate with what the token was worth.

So it does look like it was a smooth downtrend. So I wonder what that means in terms of momentum to actually reverse things. I've seen reports that whales are trying to buy more XRP to support the price. But when you see a chart like that, does it suggest that — is there a different type of tactical setup that would have to — like, does it make confirmation of a breakout harder, I guess, is my question? Because it looks like, compared to Solana or ETH or Bitcoin, all of which are also down this year, this one does seem to have the cleanest slope down.

Yeah, I would agree. I mean, it's a more decisive downtrend. And with a breakdown pending confirmation, of course, it's a bit farther away from coming close to a breakout. So it could end up sort of bringing up the rear if we do see broad-based rotation that favors the crypto market as a whole.

We really believe, at least in the equity market and top-down influences — and to maybe just a slightly lesser degree for the cryptocurrency market — with Bitcoin kind of our S&P 500, right? We want to make sure that we have that trend from Bitcoin on our side before we start going deeper down into the sort of market-cap spectrum, if you will. And so Ripple, with the shift that's more decisive than what we've seen — and then I would imagine it does stabilize, but it probably remains a laggard, because if we took the trend and looked at it relative to Bitcoin, of course, you know what you would see, right? And you want to respect the trends both in absolute and relative terms.

Hyperliquid：加密里的"半导体"

Yeah. Okay. All right. Let's touch on one more token before we start the wrap-up. Hyperliquid. Um, it's been the breakout star of, I don't know, I guess the last 12 months or so. And it is down, I think, about 28% off of its June high. Um, granted — no one better than you — um, just straight upward momentum is never sustainable, and Hyperliquid remains, as you could see on the chart, doing extremely well. But I'd love — just given how this has like a different type of chart, different dynamic than the other tokens that we talked about — I'd love to know what you're seeing here.

Well, what I'm seeing is something that looks just like the AI trade, and —

Right, or a semiconductor stock.

So if, um, you know, Bitcoin is to software, well then Hyperliquid is to semiconductors in terms of how it's been trading. And I think it does reflect sentiment around AI in a way, and just that kind of feverish investments being made ahead of what has been a pretty rough corrective phase. But that corrective phase isn't a breakdown. It does reflect a loss of upside momentum that is meaningful. But at least right now, it's not going to be long-term oversold in the same way. But there is an oversold reading on a weekly basis, and naturally on a short-term basis, that could allow for a corrective low — right? Something that has maybe shorter duration than a major low, but one that still could be tradable.

The good thing about the chart is that it can help you identify where that support is in order to have a defined risk metric, right? Because you know that if it takes out that trend line — or maybe you want to give it more room to the 200-day moving average — well, then risk is greater that this is actually more than just a correction and something that is more the start of a cyclical down move.

So you can see this kind of completely different price action. It is rare, but you can see it from the market, and there is information there. The information is probably better for a fundamental takeaway than a technical takeaway. But I just think it's fascinating how it's traded.

Hyperliquid 的竞争风险

Yeah, I'm curious. I was trying to look up quickly at the top markets on Hyperliquid to see why there is that sort of what appears to be a very high correlation. And I know there's like SpaceX, and they have SPY futures and our markets, and they have oil and other stuff too. But yeah, that certainly rings true.

And you know, I'm really curious what's going to happen with Hyperliquid. Because I mean, I'm not going to call them unregulated because I don't think that's true, and I want to really look into that before making a statement along those lines. But at the same point, it is offshore, and I do believe they geofence US users, so they can't really use the platform. But we are moving into a world where the major indices are facilitating 24/7 trading. Um, these types of perps — in any market, either through prediction markets or just through exchanges like Kraken or Coinbase or whatever — I mean, they're going to be offering regulated versions of these markets.

So for Hyperliquid, I know this isn't necessarily how you look at things, but competition is going to heat up. And I wonder — I feel like they're going to be facing the same type of challenge that Polymarket faced with Kalshi and some of these other US-based markets. Polymarket has continued to remain large even though it's been surpassed, I think, by a couple multiples in terms of Kalshi — in terms of notional open volume. But I don't know. I guess my question is, does any of that concern factor into how you would read a chart like this? Or is it really still just looking at the core momentum factors, the technical metrics that you pay attention to?

Yeah, I mean, you're talking about sort of headline risk in part. And that's something that is more prevalent for some coins. It's more prevalent for some asset classes — i.e. crude oil prices right now, right? So that'll come and go.

But to me, right now, that would be just all the more reason to have a systematic way to manage risk. So if you felt, you know, that Hyperliquid — while it has these ongoing fundamental issues, if nothing's acute — you can still trade it for a relief rally. But you would want to obviously have just that defined risk metric, whether it's a percentage-based stop-loss, watching it relative to a support level, only owning it when the MACD indicator is positive, whatever it may be. There are just ways to do that and to do it without the biases that could come with reading the news and digging into those headlines.

So for sure, overall the takeaway would be that this is a nascent sort of asset class too, and there subject to more risk and bigger swings. But then the other side of that is that with volatility there is opportunity. So I can see why people are eager to trade these instruments.

波动率：BVIV、VIX 与"制度化"

So let's finish by talking about volatility, because it's two very different pictures if you're looking at crypto. I know you talked about, um, BVIV. Actually, I'm blanking on his name, but I had him on my show last week, actually, to talk about BVIV — and sort of how it stuck in like the mid-30s, whereas volatility in indices continues to remain high, and there's been a big trend of, I would say, people irresponsibly putting money into highly leveraged ETFs.

Obviously not putting you in that category and what you offer — but I'm talking about like people in Korea putting, just dumping their life savings into these like 2x ETFs, etc., and then watching it all go away. And I'm curious, like, how you factor in those two different worlds when you're trying to make sense of charts like this.

Yeah. So, I mean, the volatility as opportunity is more a comment on the trends, and how, I guess, high-beta in a way crypto can be relative to other asset classes that have been around much longer. And it's that way with still like pretty good liquidity, right? So oftentimes you'll have less liquidity when you're looking at something that is, you know, exceptionally high-beta. So that's one way to look at it, and that would be, I think, at this time more of a positive.

Um, if you were to look at the BVIV — so, that's, I see that as just like the VIX for Bitcoin. It would be more of a gauge of sentiment in our work. We like to look at volatility via the VIX as a sort of a transactional sentiment gauge. Like, how are people feeling about this asset at this moment? And not only how are they feeling, but with that in mind, how are they positioning, right? Are they positioning for more upside or downside? And that will show if obviously they're worried about the market or not.

And where that sends a message is actually when it's at big extremes, right? So when it's just kind of like floundering and just kind of hovering, it doesn't really have a powerful takeaway, but it does when you get these extreme readings. I would argue that the BVIV, which I'm not that familiar with, it's not that extreme at this moment. If anything, it would show maybe some complacency. Uh, but that doesn't make a whole lot of sense after a downtrend. So it would be, I'd say, slightly less worrisome in terms of a complacent reading, for that reason. Like, if you saw a low reading after a big run-up, that would be a bit more concerning.

Yeah. Yeah, I've been trying to look a little bit into the reasons for the depressed BVIV — or DVOL, which is Deribit's version of the VIX. There's a couple of them out there. I know the call skew is still like relatively elevated — like people are still kind of protecting from the downside.

And there's a bit of a narrative — I'm actually curious your thoughts on this — that like the days of the 10x, 100x returns on Bitcoin and the, I guess, associated assets is over because it's become institutionalized. Is that something that you agree with?

Well, I think in becoming institutionalized, it can also be looked at a couple different ways. When I say it, I'm talking about more the uptake from asset managers — and not small ones, but the big ones. So once we see that uptake, to me that's where it also has that institutional sort of interest as an investment, right? So I don't think we're there yet. I think we actually have a really long way to go to get to the place where ultimately it should be, or could be. So there's more institutions trafficking in it, but it's not in the way that I think will necessarily contribute in a way that will minimize that volatility or tamp it down to a huge degree until we have that sort of buy-in from large, large institutions. So that's one thing.

But year-over-year, I mean, less — as we have seen — as just the asset class has been around longer, less volatility. So I think just by the nature of being around longer, to sort of oversimplify, people get more comfortable with it. I think I still get questions on, well, what happens if it's all a farce and it goes to zero? So the longer that it doesn't do that, or something extreme like that, I think the more and more, you know, sort of normalized the trends will become.

So you've seen that already in the kind of return streams to a degree. But to me there's still a whole lot of volatility to take advantage of. But then also the longer-term, that secular uptrend is established, right? We have a series of higher highs and higher lows, even though these cyclical down moves can be really dramatic.

收尾：看涨、看跌与研究获取方式

Yeah. Okay. That's a good way to put it. All right. So let's wrap up here. But before I let you go, I'd love to know if there are one or two tokens that are maybe a little under the radar that people should pay attention to, that you're keeping an eye on. And — you don't have to answer the second part — but if there's one or two that you think people should be bearish on.

Yeah. Well, I mean, I guess we'd have to focus on Ripple as the more bearish setup. We actually really focus primarily on Bitcoin and Ether in our work, because we feel that it is the most institutionally relevant, and we want to make sure that there's liquidity that we're comfortable with, market cap in a way that we're comfortable with. So we focus primarily on those.

And we feel that, again, with these signs of downside exhaustion longer term, that people should be sort of woken up right now to this improved momentum and ready to put money to work in the broader space.

So we found in building the model for our BNAV ETF that we didn't derive a lot of value from going down deeper into these altcoins without adding much more risk to the profile of the strategy. So we found that trading Bitcoin, for our purposes, was really ample, and that's where we focus.

Okay. All right. Great. Uh, well, where can people learn more about your research or yourself, if they want to follow what you put out there?

Of course. Yeah. As a place to start, our website: fairleadstrategies.com. They can receive a sample of our cryptocurrency research there. They can find more information about the two ETFs that we manage, and just generally speaking about our methodology. We also have a Twitter — or X — account, which is Stockton Katie, and people can find us that way too.

Right. It'll always be — it will always be Twitter to me.

Uh, well, with that, Katie, thanks for coming on. We'll have to have you back sometime soon. Hopefully the market's a little more volatile, and — uh, thank you to everyone for watching and listening. This will actually be my last show for a couple weeks. I'm going to be on vacation, but we'll be back in the first week in September with another exciting guest.

## 一、最反直觉的观察：Katie 的"技术派"其实是一种**认知节能装置**
表面上，Katie 用月线随机指标、Fibonacci、Demark、200 日均线这些工具"读盘"。但仔细听她的语言逻辑，你会发现她真正在做的事，不是**预测**，而是**授权自己不去思考噪音**。
她反复说：*"价格已经包含了所有信息"*、*"我们不预测明天"*、*"指标本身就带滞后，这没关系"*。
这其实是一种非常典雅的**贝叶斯懒惰**——她故意放弃对新闻、宏观、Clarity Act、硬件钱包被黑等信息的实时解读，把认知带宽全部集中在"趋势 + 动能 + 风险管理"三个变量上。这和一个禅修者的"注意力预算"分配几乎一样：*决定不看什么，比决定看什么更重要*。
对比一下：加密圈大部分分析师是"信息饕餮"，什么都想解释；Katie 是"信息素食者"，只吃价格这一种蛋白。这在一个 24/7、信息过载、叙事密度极高的加密市场里，反而成了一种**结构性优势**——不是因为她看得更准，而是因为她**决策节奏更慢**，被"叙事波动"绑架的概率更低。

item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

🎯 洞察一：市场的"信息熵定律"——为什么PCE数据永远不会引发波动

小涛无意间点出了一个市场里最反直觉的现象：PCE作为"最终结果"反而不会影响市场，而CPI/PPI作为"输入变量"却引爆行情。这背后其实是一个类似热力学第二定律的规律——信息一旦被完全推导出来，就丧失了做功能力。

更令人意外的是：这条规律揭示了一个残酷真相——大多数散户关注的"权威数据"往往是市场里最没用的数据。真正有 alpha 的信息，永远藏在"半熟的、可推导的、需要解读的"中间态里。当一个数据变得"人尽皆知它会是什么"的时候，它的市场价值就归零了。这也解释了为什么财报电话会里那些"预告性措辞"比EPS数字本身更能移动股价。

🔄 洞察二：相关性反转——市场的"生态学"隐喻

小涛讲的软件/硬件相关性反转，其实和生态学里的Lotka-Volterra 捕食者-猎物模型惊人相似。当两个物种（板块）的种群曲线过度重合（正相关趋近1）时，系统会自发地进入一个"负相关"周期以恢复平衡。

这里有一个连他自己可能都没意识到的更深层结构：他提到的"高盛一篮子交易"其实是这套生态系统的"选择压力"——它人为地制造了软件和硬件之间的资金零和博弈，就像人类活动改变了自然界的生态位。所以现在的软硬对冲已经不是自然形成的经济基本面对冲，而是华尔街量化基金集体行为塑造出来的"人工生态"。

这带来一个跨领域的启示：如果你想找到真正意义上不相关的资产，就得找那些没被主流一篮子策略"驯化"过的品种——冷门ADR、小众商品、二线加密币，因为它们没有被纳入这个人造生态系统。

💡 洞察三：黄金/真实收益率的"相变时刻"——一个物理学视角

小涛做多黄金的核心逻辑是"价格拒绝下跌"——真实收益率上涨（应该利空黄金），但黄金却在4000点站稳了。这在物理学里叫相变前兆（precursor to phase transition）：当一个系统在应该收缩的时候拒绝收缩，说明底层的规则正在改变。

最出人意料的观察是：他给出的解释——贝森特会通过操纵长债供给来压低真实收益率——其实暗示了一个更宏大的转变：美国财政部正在悄悄地从美联储手里夺走"利率定价权"。这在货币金融史上是罕见的。传统上真实收益率是市场对通胀+增长的"共识产品"，现在正在变成"财政部的政策工具"。

跨领域的启发：这和艺术品市场里"庄家操盘"的模式一模一样——当拍卖行本身开始设定价格锚点时，市场就从"价格发现"变成了"价格宣告"。黄金现在的强势，可能不是抗通胀属性，而是在下注"利率定价权的政治转移"。这是一个远比技术面、基本面都更底层的宏观赌注。

🎁 彩蛋洞察：这期视频真正教你的不是"两个技巧"

小涛表面上讲了"相关性"和"黄金分析"，但如果你把两个话题合起来看，会发现他其实在演示同一个思维方式：在极值处反向思考。CPI人尽皆知时找PPI里的细节；相关性趋近1时押注反转；市场认为最鹰派时押注鸽派转向。这是一种"永远和共识保持一个身位差"的哲学——它不是技术分析、不是基本面分析，是共识的元分析。

📝 转录文本

【投资TALK君1472期】相关性风控 + 黄金逻辑

开场

各位观众大家好，欢迎来到一个每天不单只聊新闻的专业美股频道，我是市场分析师小涛。

今天这期内容主要教大家两个小技巧、两个思路吧——也不算两个小技巧：

  • 第一个思路：怎么通过两个标的之间的相关性、或者两个指数之间的相关性，去进行仓位上的管理。
  • 第二个思路：从过去这段时间的走势去判断一下接下去黄金的走势，包括为什么我在两周多之前开始做多黄金背后的理由到底是什么。

好吗？那我就废话不多说了，直接开始。

那在开始之前，大家记得留言、点赞加转发，让更多的人可以看到我们这期内容，让留言区里面的机器人没有容身之地。

一、PPI 数据解读与 PCE 预判

先来看一下，今天先两组数据说一下。

第一组数据就是早上所公布——周四早上所公布的 PPI 数据。那 PPI 数据是好于市场的这个预期，数据发布完之后，其实整个标普，无论是硬件软件都出现了一个反弹，一开始是有一些追涨的一个趋势，然后之后的话出现了一些板块之间的分歧。

有了 CPI 数据，我们有了 PPI 数据，全部加在一起，其实对于 7 月份的 PCE 数据就已经有了这个结果了。市场的这一个预期——其实这一个不是预期啊，就市场计算出来这个结果——七月份的核心 PCE 环比增速是在 0.22%，上一个月是 0.13%。所以这一个月的数据其实没有上个月要好。

那严格意义上来说，如果我们把 0.22 把它年化的话，那同比的增速也在 2.7%，2.7% 也并没有达到美联储 2% 的这个通胀目标。那要达到 2% 的通胀目标，PCE 或者通胀指数环比增速差不多是在 0.18% 左右。

所以就像 CPI 指数出来之后，我的一个观点就是：你说这组数据本身市场可以接受吗？可以接受。这也是为什么数据发布完之后，无论是 CPI 数据还是 PPI 数据，发布完数据之后，九月份加息的这个概率都降低了。但是还是有一定的概率九月份会加息，因为在九月份的联储会议之前，我们还会看到下一个月或者下一组的 CPI 通胀数据。

为什么 PCE 数据发布时市场毫无反应？

好吗？然后另外一点我想强调的是——因为 PCE 的数据会在每一个月的月底才公布，而我发现市场里面还是有一部分的人，包括有一些自媒体在关注，觉得"哎，这一组 PPI、这一组 PCE 数据会对于市场造成什么的一些影响"。

回过头你会发现，每一次公布 PCE 数据的时候，市场根本就不会有任何的波动和反应。为什么？是因为该有的这个反应全部在公布 CPI 数据和 PPI 数据的时候已经做出反应了。因为 PCE 数据是 PPI 数据和 CPI 数据出来之后的一个计算结果，PCE 数据它并不是一个预期，简单来说就现在市场预计 PCE 数据会停在 0.2，基本上最终的这个结果就是在 0.2，前后的这个误差不会超过 0.01%。

好吗？所以我们要知道到底哪些数据对于市场是有影响的，而并不是每一组的宏观数据我们都需要去花非常多的时间去关注。

二、市场参与度更新与仓位逻辑分层

然后就是市场的参与度，我再来做一个更新。

我昨天在 X 上嘛，我有发过——我今天我在 X 上我有发过，我说接下去整个市场这边，我们从仓位这个角度，我们就继续持有，然后等待这个市场参与度去到一个超买的这个位置，然后我们才去思考是不是要稍微小心一些。

逻辑分层

超卖的这个思路也是停在估值的思路下面：

  1. 整个如果我们去看美股的估值，估值一定是最高的这个逻辑层面；
  2. 然后接下去我们可以从个别标的去看个别标的这个估值；
  3. 再往下去看，可能一些宏观的数据、或者市场的一个参与度，可能会给我们一些参考的——就操作上可能或者仓位上的一个调整，可能会有一些参考的意义；
  4. 再下去的话就是一些技术指标。

那所以每一层每一层的逻辑我们一定要分清楚。当两层不同的逻辑之间出现不同信号的时候，我们要知道哪一个逻辑到底是一个主观的一个判断标准。

举例：为什么当时不应该减仓软件板块

那么举个例子，就像如果个别标的它的估值仍然是在一个低位，那即使参与度去到了一个非常高的位置，那这时候对于这些个别标的需不需要去减仓？不需要去减仓，对吧？

最好的一个例子就是前段时间。那么当硬件板块在下跌的时候，市场非常的恐慌，然后有人问我，他说指数还没有下跌，当指数下跌的时候，那是不是软件板块还会跟着一起下跌？

我说没有任何的理由在那个位置去减仓软件板块，因为我们知道软件板块现金流非常的好，且又没有资本开支，又不花钱，然后估值又在一个低位，为什么在这个位置要去减仓软件板块？这就是一个非常标准的从基本面这个角度去出发的这个判断，和当时市场怎么去走、哪些标的在下跌完全没有任何的关系，对吗？

而只要那时候听进我一些劝的话，你起码在软件板块，在过去这段时间，你就不会去割肉割掉。那过去这段时间，其实软件板块的涨幅或者反弹是远远好于硬件板块。

当前参与度水位

好吧，所以回到参与度这边，那经过周四整个市场的一个反弹之后：

  • 纳指现在也是开始出现了一个中性偏乐观的位置；
  • 罗素 2000 和标普 500 基本上现在接近于超买的位置。

超买的话，我把它定义为——如果参与度在 70% 以上，就进入一个超买的区间。那什么时候是一个警戒的位置？当 20 日均线和 50 日均线都去到 75% 至 80% 之间、甚至到 80% 以上的话，就绝对是一个警戒的一个区间了。

三、思路一：用相关性做仓位管理（软件 vs 硬件）

那么聊完这些数据之后，我们来看第一个我想和大家分享的一个思路。

日内观察：Workday 消息与板块联动

首先这张图里两条线：

  • 蓝色这条线是 IGV（软件板块）的一个 ETF；
  • 白色这条线是 SOXX（芯片板块）的 ETF。

那我这边看的是日内的走势。因为今天我正好看到社交媒体上我看到一张图，他聊的是为什么——因为我们知道在周四的时候，周四的下午，Workday 出现了一条新闻，Workday 有可能被收购，然后最多最高的时候盘中一度上涨了 20% 多，并且把整个软件板块全部带起来了。

因为 Workday 一家公司有可能会被收购，把所有软件板块全部带起来，其实是完全不合理的一种结果。那完全不合理，对吗？

那之所以会出现这种情况，就是我最近这段时间一直影响市场的一个主线条——高盛的一个一篮子股票。那这个一篮子股票或者背后交易的一个逻辑就是：某一个时间段，这一个交易的逻辑线会成为市场里边交易的一个主流的一个逻辑线。

比如说做空硬件：当硬件下跌的时候，软件就得上涨；当软件下跌的时候，硬件就得上涨。所以在周四下午的时候，我们可以看到非常明显的这种走势——蓝色这条线，被收购的这条消息出来之后，IGV 一波暴涨；接下去看到 IGV 持续上涨，白色这条线 SOXX 芯片板块就持续下跌。

那在这段时间，如果我们去看这一个相关性——因为我这边是一分钟的 K 线图，那我这边看的是过去 5 个交易日或者过去 5 个交易的时间点。一分钟的话，就是过去 5 分钟。在滚动 5 分钟的这段时间里边，基本上下午后两点多之后，一直出现一个负相关，就是软件板块和硬件板块之间一直是一个负相关的走势，或者这个主流的这个逻辑线一直是市场里面的主流。

日线级别：相关性极值与反转信号

那我讲这些东西有什么意义呢？有意义。

如果我们把时间线调到日 K 线，然后我看 YTD 到现在为止这个走势，同样和前面一样——SOXX 白色这条线是芯片板块，然后蓝色这条线是 IGV 软件板块，同样的还是 5 个交易区间。

那从 5 个交易日这个角度去看，滚动 5 个交易日这个角度去看，可以看到：从今年的 4 月份、5 月份、6 月份，基本上不断地会出现两者之间的这个负相关。

我给大家举一个经典的一个时间点——6 月中旬的时候，我们看到非常正相关，一度这个正相关达到了 100%。那当我们看到这两者之间非常正相关的时候，就代表在过去这段时间——从 6 月初到 6 月中旬这段时间——你可以看到这两者之间是几乎大家一起上涨和一起下跌。

那当出现一起上涨一起下跌的时候，有可能这段时间的一个走势受到了一些整个市场的一些影响，或者宏观因素的一些影响。那这时候，当我们看到一个相关性在极端的时候，那比如说非常接近于正相关、非常接近于 1，或者负相关非常接近于负一的时候，我们知道接下去有可能会出现什么——就一个相关性会出现一个反转。

当相关性出现反转，就当相关性接近于 1 的时候，接下去出现反转的话，那就代表这两者之间会出走势上会出现一个负相关。那所以在 6 月中旬以后，我们看到这两者之间确实出现了一个负相关。那负相关体现在：芯片板块出现了反弹去摸了一个新高，然后软件板块继续下跌。

如何用相关性指导加仓时点

那观察这种相关性对于我们来说有什么帮助？有帮助。

就像我前面提到的，比如说当我们选择在加仓的时候：如果我自己现在手里所持有的一些个股，比如说硬件比较多的话，哎，我正好看到一个软件板块里边的标的估值非常的便宜，然后我又愿意去加仓，那这时候你可以去等一个什么——可以去等一个诶，这两者之间的相关性在一个非常正相关的时候，你可以去选择进行加仓这一个软件板块。

因为如果在选择在那个时候进行加仓的话，接下去有可能会发生的情况是——你所加仓的这个软件板块的标的会和你已经持有的硬件板块的标的出现一个负相关，彼此之间出现一个对冲。

  • 如果我们做交易的话，那你可以看比如说我这边的日 K 线，然后滚动 5 日的相关性，或者滚动 10 日的相关性；
  • 如果做投资的话，其实我们可以把这个相关性滚动的一个相关性时间线拉长，滚动 20 日、滚动 30 日都可以去看。

软硬双修：今年的核心配置理念

这其实也是今年我一直强调的：在我们做资产配置选标的的时候，要做到一个什么——软硬双修，就是软件也要、硬件也要。因为这两者之间你看非常多的时间之内出现一个负相关，那这时候负相关的时候，嗯，当指数在下跌的时候，当硬件在下跌的时候，你会发现，哎，软件就起到了一个非常好的、对于整体投资组合的一个支撑的作用。

那比如说今年 7 月份以来的这波走势最明显：那 7 月份硬件板块出现了下跌，但软件板块其实表现得非常的强势。在 8 月份、7 月底 8 月份的时候，软件板块的反弹幅度远远好于硬件。

我这边只是拿了这两个指数出来给了一个参考。那我知道大多数的人我们在做资产配置的时候不会往这个角度去思考，那我这边只是给大家分享一个思路，加了更多的一个维度进来，那么在我们去选择标的的时候，多一层的一个思考在背后。

四、思路二：黄金走势与真实收益率的负相关

那么我们来聊下黄金。

加仓黄金的第一个观察：价格拒绝下跌

那我在两周之前开始加仓黄金的时候，我和大家分享过一个思路。当时其实正好我是扫到——首先我们知道黄金和美债，特别是 10 年期美债的一个真实收益率是一个负相关。

那图里： - 白色这条线是黄金的一个价格走势； - 蓝色这条线就是 10 年期美国国债的一个真实收益率。

我都不用把相关性拉出来，大家从走势上就可以看到这两者之间比较明显的一个负相关。那么当白色上涨的时候蓝色下跌，当蓝色下跌的时候白色上涨。

那我在两周多之前，我看到这条线的时候，我发现一个问题：就是当白色这条线——黄金这个价格、黄金这个走势——在 4000 点的时候，得到了一个非常强的一个支撑；同时我们发现蓝色这条线——美国国债的一个真实收益率一路在上涨。

也就是我们在整个七月份、六月底到七月份这段时间看到的是——美债的一个真实收益率一路在上涨。理论上来说，对于黄金来说应该是一个利空。但是价格却告诉我们跌不下去了。这是第一个观察。

第二个观察：Peak Hawkishness（最鹰派时刻已过）

然后第二个观察，并且当时是在上一次的美联储会议之前，我选择的加仓。

很多人不理解说：你觉得美联储要加息，那你为什么要去加仓黄金？加息理论上来说不是会变得更加的鹰派吗？有可能会使得真实收益率继续上涨。

那但是我说过，市场已经定价了将近今年两次的一个加息幅度，已经不可能再鹰了——除非我们认为今年会加息三次，或今年会加息两次以上或者加息三次，那我们认为这个鹰派还有空间在哪边。但是如果我——因为我个人认为最多就加息两次，不可能加了超过两次，就没有这个空间在那边。

那如果说他选择进行加息，反而对于偿债这一块的真实收益率是一个利好——就他有可能会出现下降。我们叫 peak hawkishness，就最鹰派的这个时间点有可能就在身后，或者就是那一次的美联储会议。

那结果那一次美联储会议出来之后，它是非常的鸽派，也就说理论上来说，最鹰派的这个时间点是上一次，是 6 月份的美联储会议，对吧？这算是当时一个思路吧。

8 月走势验证与后续空间

然后我们看下整个 8 月份：8 月份黄金的反弹幅度是比较的强，差不多最低点到这，我差不多 8%~9%，一度的话百超过 10%。那蓝色这条线真实收益率其实下降了，但是下降的这个幅度没有那么的明显。

那么接下去 10 年期美国国债的一个真实收益率有没有继续下跌这个空间呢？如果继续下跌的话，那黄金这个价格理论上还有继续上涨这个空间在那边，对吗？

那我个人的看法是有这个空间在那边。

什么东西影响到 10 年期美债真实收益率的话，我在可能几期视频前面我有特地聊过，这边我就不多做展开。主要的一个原因，我认为有可能会影响到真实收益率继续下跌的是——美国财政部这边对于长债收益率这一块继续上涨已经没办法容忍，所以贝森特选择出来进行干预。

那包括接下去有可能会看到他们在融资这一块偏向于短债，而并不是长债。比较简单的一个思考方式呢——如果说 10 年期的通胀预期不变的话，那长债这一块的一个融资体量就供给端这一块稍微减少一些，使得名义利率出现下降，那真实收益率也会出现下降。

好吗？所以如果黄金这段时间我看一下，现在 4350、4370 左右——如果黄金有一个 pullback 的话，可能黄金会是另外一个短期之内从交易这个角度去看，会是一个另外一个进场点。

好吧，那希望前面两个思路的一个分享对大家有帮助。

五、APP 大整改预告

那最后今天的活动是我的 APP。APP 在下一周就会进行一个大整改了，这一次整改完之后是面目全非，往好的一个方向去了。

那主要就是解决几个问题啊：

1. 连接和稳定度

那么以前需要用 VPN 的，现在 VPN 也不需要了（除了你看油管的视频需要 VPN 以外）。

2. 加入 Forward PE

然后还加入了 forward PE。那今年我说，上一年如果我们要了解一个 beta 的这个概念，今年就是 forward PE。今年的 forward PE 已经好几次，无论从指数还是从个股，帮助我们去进行减仓和加仓。

包括在市场下跌的时候，PE——那么 forward PE 才是我们坚定可以去加仓的一个非常好的一个标准。那当 forward PE 在低位的时候，我们敢去加仓，很多人都在留言区里面最后给我这样的一个反馈——PE 给了他们支撑；那么 PE 在高的时候让他们去减仓，给了他们减仓的这个理由。

所以 forward PE 也会加进来，指数、个股都会有。

3. 绩效和个股页

然后新加的一个功能就是绩效和个股页。大家知道我所有的操作全部会在 APP 里面第一时间和大家分享。

那包括了在过去这一个月里面： - 从基本面加仓了一些标的，比如说 BE、比如说诺基亚等等，那这段时间其实走的还好，反弹没有非常的好，但还是不错的； - 然后一些交易的一些标的，过去这两周两个交易的标的也非常的好——一个是 NUGT 36%，然后另外一个是昨天刚刚选择清仓的 NBIS。这一波很多人在讨论 Nebius 财报等等，但是我们在 Nebius 财报之前就已经进去布局了。

那么所以我所有的操作，然后包括 YTD 的一些走势回报、包括整个 portfolio 的一个贝塔都会在 APP 里面和大家分享。包括大家把自己的仓位投资组合放进去之后，可以和我的进行对比。

下载方式

所以这一次 APP 是一个全面的一个大整改。希望以前如果没有用过的，在下周上线完之后可以来用一下；以前如果用过的、觉得不满意的，我也希望大家在下一周上线完之后可以来用一下。即使不加入会员，也有很多的一些免费功能，我觉得是非常有价值的。

那会员的话，现在是一个早鸟的价格，一年是 569 美金。下载的方式，大家可以通过这个二维码，或者在置顶留言里面的这个链接，用手机登录就可以进行下载。或者你直接去苹果谷歌商店搜索"投资 talk 君"也可以搜到这个 APP。

好吗？那今天这期内容到这边，我们下期见。

## 🎯 洞察一：市场的"信息熵定律"——为什么PCE数据永远不会引发波动
小涛无意间点出了一个市场里最反直觉的现象：**PCE作为"最终结果"反而不会影响市场，而CPI/PPI作为"输入变量"却引爆行情**。这背后其实是一个类似**热力学第二定律**的规律——信息一旦被完全推导出来，就丧失了做功能力。
更令人意外的是：这条规律揭示了一个残酷真相——**大多数散户关注的"权威数据"往往是市场里最没用的数据**。真正有 alpha 的信息，永远藏在"半熟的、可推导的、需要解读的"中间态里。当一个数据变得"人尽皆知它会是什么"的时候，它的市场价值就归零了。这也解释了为什么财报电话会里那些"预告性措辞"比EPS数字本身更能移动股价。
## 🔄 洞察二：相关性反转——市场的"生态学"隐喻
小涛讲的软件/硬件相关性反转，其实和生态学里的**Lotka-Volterra 捕食者-猎物模型**惊人相似。当两个物种（板块）的种群曲线过度重合（正相关趋近1）时，系统会自发地进入一个"负相关"周期以恢复平衡。

item.title: [Lex Clips] Why Khabib beat up Lex in training
item.dc:creator: Lex Clips
item.content:encoded:
💡 创造性洞见

一个反直觉的观察：Khabib 偷走了他"讨厌"的武术灵魂

大多数人听到 Khabib 说"我不喜欢合气道，但我喜欢它的哲学"时会一带而过，可这句话其实揭示了一种极其罕见的元认知能力——他能够把一门学科的"美学表达"和"底层逻辑"完全剥离开。绝大多数格斗家的态度是二元的：要么全盘吸收（如 BJJ 信徒），要么彻底鄙视（如许多摔跤手对付花式踢击的态度）。而 Khabib 做的是一件更接近哲学家而非武者的事情：从他鄙视的东西里提炼精华，再嫁接到他崇拜的东西上。这也解释了为什么他能同时是最"传统"的达吉斯坦摔跤手，又是最"现代"的 MMA 综合体——他的兼容性来自于蔑视表面、只取内核。

Top Pressure 的真相：那不是身体压制，是"代谢破产"攻击

采访里 Khabib 说的"重压"表面看是关于体重和力量，但仔细听他描述——"迫使对手进入他们必须逃脱、必须消耗能量的位置"——你会意识到他真正在描述的是一场能量经济战。他不是在压碎你的骨头，他是在提高你每一次呼吸、每一次挣扎的单位价格。这与国际象棋里的 Zugzwang（无路可走）几乎完全同构：不是把对手将死，而是让对手的每一步棋都恶化自己的处境。也与网络安全里的 DDoS 攻击同构：不是攻破系统，而是让系统在处理无效请求中耗尽资源。

更进一步，这在商业世界里对应的是 Bezos 式的"让竞争对手的利润率变成你的机会"——通过不断提高对手维持现状的成本，让他们主动放弃战场。Khabib 的降服往往发生在第三、第四回合，不是因为他那时才变强，而是因为对手的"预算"到那时才耗尽。

那只"咬住弱点的狗"：达吉斯坦爷爷讲的是进化论

Khabib 引用祖父的话——"咬住一个弱点不放的狗总能赢"——听起来像温情的家庭智慧，但这实际上是一句极其残酷的进化生物学声明。自然界里，掠食者从不"公平决斗"。狼群不挑最强的驼鹿，它们挑跛脚的那只；猎豹追踪的是掉队的羚羊；病毒攻击的是免疫系统的裂缝。

这与体育文化崇尚的"直面对手最强项"叙事完全相反——观众爱看拳王对拳王的对轰，可 Khabib 反问："为什么我要和 Conor 站着打？"这句话里藏着一个几乎所有人都在职业生涯某个时刻违背过的原则：你的"荣誉感"往往是你最大的战略敌人。这也解释了硅谷创业教父们反复说的"不要在巨头强项上竞争"——从 Airbnb 不去建酒店，到 Netflix 不去开影院，本质上都是那只咬弱点的狗。

一个隐藏联系：Khabib 的哲学与"精益创业"惊人同源

把 Khabib 的三个原则并列——① 用对手的力反制对手、② 迫使对手在无效动作上消耗资源、③ 找到弱点持续施压——你会发现这几乎逐字对应了 Eric Ries《精益创业》的核心：① Pivot（借力转向）、② 消除 Waste（浪费）、③ 找到 Product-Market Fit 的关键杠杆并 all-in。一位达吉斯坦山村长大的摔跤手，和一位斯坦福 MBA 提出的方法论，在最底层的"资源不对称下的胜利路径"上是同一张地图。这或许暗示了一个更大的真相：任何领域的顶级掌控者，最终都在解同一道数学题——如何用最小的能量输出，制造最大的对方能量塌陷。

📝 转录文本

On Top Pressure and the Aikido Philosophy

Interviewer: Can you break down the technical details of your top pressure? That pressure you put on in wrestling, on the ground, all of it. How does it work? Can you explain the philosophy behind it?

Khabib: Well, over the years, I have learned to use my strength properly. There's this sport called Aikido. I don't like it much, but I like their philosophy, where your strength might work against you.

I think for a lot of listeners, this is going to be a brand new sport, but there is this sport called Aikido, and the whole philosophy behind it is using your opponent's force against them. That's what I learned to do. And I have learned to force an opponent into positions where they have to escape wasting their energy.

The Sparring Session — A Deliberate Message

Like when we were sparring yesterday —

Interviewer: Mhm.

Khabib: — that's exactly what I wanted. I wanted you to feel that energy, that heavy top pressure. We could have just played around. I could have gone easy on you, but I wanted you to feel the real heavy pressure. And of course, please don't think it was a sign of disrespect. It's quite the opposite.

Interviewer: No, it was respect.

Khabib: I just wanted you to feel that, you know, how exhausting it can be. I think you felt it yourself that it was a bit different from the kind of grappling you've dealt with before. I'm sure of it.

Interviewer: The only one who's even close to that is — I mean, you're the absolute number one, but the only thing is when I trained with Roger Gracie in a different sport, you get that same feeling with him. Like the guy is just insanely heavy.

Khabib: Mhm. Pressure. Pressure. Well, Roger, he's the greatest, too. He's the greatest in his own sport.

Style, Dedication, and Craft

What makes a person unique is his style, his style and his approach to his work. I always approach my craft very professionally, you know, respectfully. I believe that if you're going to be in this game in this sport, you have to completely dedicate yourself to it.

Interviewer: But, I think you had a deep understanding of how to break an opponent both physically and psychologically. Just looking at your style.

The Grandfather's Lesson — Latch onto the Weakness

Khabib: I've always been right there, always fighting for position. I always — look, I mean — I just always had this thought in my head. My grandfather always told me, "A dog that latches onto that one weak spot always wins."

It's the same with a fighter. When you're fighting on pure instinct, you feel your opponent's weakness. You know where they're weak, and you have to keep pressing right there.

Applying the Principle — The Conor Example

For example, let's say I'm fighting Conor, right? His strengths are his striking, his timing, and his speed. His boxing. Why would I stand and strike with him? What am I supposed to do? I have to put pressure on his weak spot.

So, uh, that's what separates the fighters who reach success, the highest level of success, and become the best of the best. They — they know how to find an opponent's weakness, and they pressure it relentlessly.

So, so, it all comes down to having the right strategy here.
